examples.en: Women's groups welcomed the new bill.
Figures from women's circles gathered for a meeting.
The voice of the women's community is getting louder.

examples.ko: 이번 정책에 대해 여성계가 입장을 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The women's community stated its position on this policy.
She is a person respected in women's circles.
Women's groups and the government have started talks.

explain: 뉴스나 신문에서 여성 문제와 관련된 단체와 인사들을 한데 묶어 말할 때 써요. '정계, 재계, 문화계'처럼 '-계'가 붙어 어떤 분야의 사람들 전체를 가리키는 말과 같은 틀이에요.

phrases.en: Figures from the women's community gave their opinions to the government.
phrases.nuance_ko: 여성 문제에 관여하는 사람들을 뉴스에서 부를 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used in the news for people involved in women's issues.

phrases.en: The reaction from women's circles is mostly positive.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어떤 일에 대한 해당 분야의 반응을 전할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to report how that field reacted to something.

phrases.en: The voice of women's groups is getting louder.
phrases.nuance_ko: 요구나 주장이 강해질 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing used when demands or claims grow stronger.

explain_en: It appears in news and newspapers to group together organizations and figures involved in women's issues. It follows the same pattern as '정계', '재계' and '문화계', where '-계' refers to everyone in a particular field.

en: to go against; to run counter to; to retrogress

examples.en: That policy goes against the trend of the times.

examples.ko: 물가는 오르는데 월급은 줄다니 상식에 역행하는 일이에요.
examples.en: Prices go up while wages drop, which goes against common sense.
Time never runs backward.

examples.ko: 이 법은 국민의 바람에 역행한다는 비판을 받았어요.
examples.en: This law was criticized for going against what the people want.

examples.ko: 저는 유행에 역행해서 오래된 옷만 입어요.
examples.en: I go against trends and only wear old clothes.
Swimming against the current is very tiring.

explain: '시대·흐름·추세에 역행하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 쓰는 경우가 많아요. 좋지 않다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요. 도로에서 반대 방향으로 달리는 것은 보통 '역주행'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: That decision goes against the global trend.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-에 역행하다'로 흐름과 반대로 간다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: '-에 역행하다' means going against a trend.

phrases.en: People opposed the policy that goes backward.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-는'으로 뒤의 명사를 꾸며서 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses '-는' to modify a noun, often when criticizing.

phrases.example: 우리 계획이 자꾸 거꾸로 가는 것 같아요.
phrases.en: It feels like our plan keeps going backward.
phrases.nuance_ko: '역행하다'를 쉽게 풀어 쓴 일상 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An everyday paraphrase of '역행하다'.

explain_en: Formal, negative — moving against time, trend or progress (시대에 역행하다) It is often used with the particle '에', as in '시대·흐름·추세에 역행하다' (go against the times or trend), and it carries a critical tone. Driving the wrong way on a road is usually called '역주행'.

en: the price of fame; toll of being a celebrity

examples.ko: 유명세 때문에 마음대로 외출을 못 해요.
examples.en: Because of the price of fame, going out freely is hard.
Stars are bound to pay the price of fame.
As the fame grew, privacy shrank.
With more popularity comes the price of fame.

examples.ko: 어디를 가도 사진을 찍히는 것도 유명세예요.
examples.en: Being photographed wherever you go is also part of the price of fame.

examples.ko: 유명세에 지쳐서 가수가 잠깐 쉬기로 했어요.
examples.en: Worn out by the burdens of fame, the singer decided to take a short break.

explain: '인기'는 사람들이 좋아하는 것이고, '유명세'는 유명해진 대가로 겪는 불편이에요. 그래서 '유명세를 치르다'처럼 '치르다'와 함께 써요. 사생활 침해나 악플 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 그 배우는 유명세를 톡톡히 치르고 있어요.
phrases.en: That actor is paying a heavy price for fame.
phrases.nuance_ko: '톡톡히'를 넣으면 불편이 꽤 크다는 뜻이 강해져요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 톡톡히 stresses that the trouble is quite big.

phrases.en: Celebrities sometimes suffer from the price of fame.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유명해서 생기는 불편이 계속될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the trouble from being famous goes on.

phrases.example: 유명세 때문에 길에서 자꾸 사진이 찍혀요.
phrases.en: Because of my fame, people keep taking my picture on the street.
phrases.nuance_ko: 유명해서 생긴 불편의 이유를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to give fame as the reason for a trouble.

explain_en: '인기' is being liked by many people, while '유명세' is the inconvenience you suffer as the cost of being famous. That is why it goes with '치르다' (to pay): '유명세를 치르다'. It often comes up in talk about privacy invasion and malicious comments.

en: to let something fizzle out; to leave unresolved

examples.ko: 그 문제는 책임자 없이 유야무야 넘어간 적이 많아요.
examples.en: That issue has often been brushed aside with no one taking responsibility.
That case ended up fizzling out without a clear conclusion.

examples.ko: 회의 결과가 유야무야해서 아무도 책임지지 않아요.
examples.en: The meeting result is vague, so nobody takes responsibility.
The start was loud, but the end just fizzled out.
That matter dragged on vaguely and was eventually forgotten.

examples.ko: 숙제를 유야무야 넘기면 나중에 더 힘들어요.
examples.en: If you let your homework slide without dealing with it, it gets harder later.

explain: 큰 문제나 사건이 분명한 결론 없이 흐지부지 끝나는 모습에 써요. 실제로는 '유야무야 넘어가다', '유야무야 끝나다'처럼 쓰는 일이 많고, 일상에서는 '흐지부지'라고도 말해요. 좋지 않은 일을 비판할 때 자주 어울려요.

phrases.example: 이번 잘못이 유야무야 넘어가면 안 돼요.
phrases.en: This mistake must not be allowed to slide without being settled.
phrases.nuance_ko: 분명하게 정리하지 않고 그냥 지나갈 때 가장 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common collocation for letting something pass without clear resolution.

phrases.en: The investigation just fizzled out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 결론 없이 일이 저절로 끝나는 모습을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes something ending on its own with no conclusion.

phrases.en: My exercise plan fizzled out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '유야무야' 대신 쓰는 편한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual everyday alternative to '유야무야'.

explain_en: It describes a big problem or incident that fades away without a clear conclusion. It is often used in forms like '유야무야 넘어가다' and '유야무야 끝나다', and in daily talk people also say '흐지부지'. It fits well when criticizing something unsatisfactory.

examples.ko: 이번 선거에서 그 당의 의석수가 크게 늘었어요.
examples.en: In this election, that party's number of seats grew a lot.

examples.ko: 의석수가 많은 정당이 법안을 통과시키기 쉬워요.
examples.en: A party with many seats can pass bills more easily.
The two parties have almost the same number of seats.
The negotiations dragged on over the number of seats.
The ruling party tried hard to keep its seats.
The party leader resigned because the seat count fell.

explain: 선거 뉴스에서 자주 나오는 말이에요. '의석'은 자리 하나하나를, '의석수'는 그 개수를 말해요. '의석을 얻다/잃다/차지하다'처럼 '의석'과 함께 알아 두면 좋아요.

phrases.example: 이번 선거에서 우리 당의 의석수가 늘었어요.
phrases.en: Our party's number of seats increased in this election.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선거 결과를 말할 때 쓰고, 반대말은 '줄다'예요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for election results; the opposite is 줄다.

phrases.example: 그 정당은 절반이 넘는 의석을 차지했어요.
phrases.en: That party took more than half of the seats.
phrases.nuance_ko: '의석수'가 개수라면 이 표현은 자리를 얻는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: While 의석수 is the count, this phrase describes winning the seats.

phrases.en: Several parties lost seats in the election.
phrases.nuance_ko: 선거에서 졌을 때 쓰는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when parties lose seats in an election.

explain_en: It appears often in election news. '의석' is each individual seat, and '의석수' is the count of them. It helps to learn it together with '의석' in phrases like '의석을 얻다/잃다/차지하다'.

examples.ko: 이 사찰은 창건 이야기가 아주 흥미로워요.
examples.en: The story of how this temple was founded is very interesting.
This temple marks the 1,300th anniversary of its founding this year.

examples.ko: 안내문에는 사찰의 창건 시기가 적혀 있어요.
examples.en: The information sign states when the temple was founded.

examples.ko: 이 탑은 절의 창건과 함께 세워졌다고 해요.
examples.en: They say this pagoda was built along with the founding of the temple.

examples.ko: 창건 당시의 모습은 지금과 많이 달랐어요.
examples.en: Its appearance at the time of its founding was very different from now.
An event was held to commemorate the founding of the country.

explain: '창건'은 절, 왕조, 나라처럼 역사적이고 큰 것을 처음 세울 때 써요. 회사나 학교, 단체에는 '창립'이나 '설립'이 더 자연스러워요. 일상 대화보다는 관광 안내문이나 역사 설명에서 자주 보여요.

phrases.en: This temple's founding legend is interesting.
phrases.nuance_ko: 절이나 나라가 처음 세워진 이야기를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: A story about how a temple or country was first founded.

phrases.example: 이 궁궐의 창건 시기를 알고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to know when this palace was founded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 세워진 때를 물을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to ask when something was first built.

phrases.example: 이 절은 창건 이래 한 번도 문을 닫지 않았어요.
phrases.en: Since its founding, this temple has never closed.
phrases.nuance_ko: 처음 세워진 뒤로 지금까지라는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means from the time of founding until now.

explain_en: Founding of a temple, palace or country; historical tone. '창건' is used when a historically significant thing such as a temple, a dynasty or a nation is first established. For companies, schools or organizations, '창립' or '설립' sounds more natural. You will see it more in tourist signs and history explanations than in everyday talk.

t90.ax: The information sign states when the temple was founded.

en: to decide; to determine; to judge

examples.ko: 이번 경기가 우승 팀을 판가름하게 돼요.
examples.en: This match will decide the winning team.
The final vote will determine the result.
What decides the outcome is stamina in the end.
It's not easy to judge who is right.
The referee's call decided the match.
This interview determines whether you pass.

explain: '결정하다'보다 두 갈래 중 어느 쪽인지 갈리는 순간에 잘 어울려요. 승부, 합격, 옳고 그름에 많이 써요. '판가름이 나다'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: The match was decided by the last goal.
phrases.nuance_ko: 승부나 결과가 마침내 정해졌다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to say that a result or outcome was finally settled.

phrases.en: The last question decided the outcome.
phrases.nuance_ko: 이기고 지는 것을 정하는 중요한 일을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an important thing that decides who wins or loses.

phrases.example: 두 팀 실력이 비슷해서 누가 이길지 판가름하기 어려워요.
phrases.en: The two teams are so evenly matched that it's hard to tell who will win.
phrases.nuance_ko: '-기 어렵다'를 붙여 결과를 쉽게 알 수 없다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: With -기 어렵다, it says the result is hard to call.

explain_en: To decide the outcome of a contest or issue; slightly literary. Compared with '결정하다', it fits moments when things split into two outcomes. It is often used for the result of a match, pass or fail, and right or wrong. People also commonly say '판가름이 나다'.

t90.ax: It's not easy to judge who is right.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 패전 이후 경제를 다시 일으켰어요.
examples.en: After its defeat in the war, that country rebuilt its economy.

examples.ko: 패전 소식이 전해지자 사람들은 크게 낙담했어요.
examples.en: When the news of the defeat spread, people were greatly discouraged.
The coach stepped down, taking responsibility for the defeat.
As defeats piled up, the soldiers' morale fell.
In history class, we learned about the situation of the defeated country.

examples.ko: 어제 경기에서 그 투수가 패전 투수가 됐어요.
examples.en: In yesterday's game, that pitcher became the losing pitcher.

explain: 전쟁에서 진 일을 말해서 역사 수업이나 뉴스에서 자주 나오고, 반대말은 '승전'이에요. 야구에서는 '패전 투수'처럼도 써요.

phrases.example: 패전국은 전쟁 뒤에 많은 것을 잃었어요.
phrases.en: The defeated nation lost a lot after the war.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전쟁에서 진 나라를 말하고, 반대는 '승전국'이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A country that lost a war; the opposite is 승전국.

phrases.example: 어제 경기에서 그 선수가 패전 투수가 됐어요.
phrases.en: In yesterday's game, that player became the losing pitcher.
phrases.nuance_ko: 야구에서 진 경기의 책임을 진 투수를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In baseball, the pitcher charged with the loss.

phrases.en: The whole country fell silent at the news of the defeat.
phrases.nuance_ko: 전쟁에서 졌다는 소식을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for news that a war has been lost.

explain_en: Losing a war or battle — formal, history and news. It refers to losing a war, so it often appears in history lessons and the news, and the opposite is '승전'. In baseball it is also used as in '패전 투수' (losing pitcher).

en: to equalize; to level; to standardize

examples.ko: 정부는 학교 사이의 격차를 평준화하려고 해요.
examples.en: The government is trying to even out the gaps between schools.

examples.ko: 임금을 평준화하면 불만이 줄어들 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If wages are leveled out, complaints might decrease.
We even out skill levels so the game is fair.

examples.ko: 모든 매장의 서비스를 평준화하는 것이 목표예요.
examples.en: The goal is to standardize the service at all stores.
Someone suggested that prices be equalized.

examples.ko: 팀을 나눌 때 실력을 평준화해 주세요.
examples.en: Please balance skill levels when you split the teams.

explain: '같게 하다'보다 높낮이 차이를 줄여 고르게 맞춘다는 느낌이에요. 학교, 임금, 서비스처럼 격차가 있는 것을 비슷한 수준으로 맞출 때 써요. 격차가 줄어드는 결과는 '평준화'로 말해요.

phrases.en: We have to equalize the gaps between schools.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해야 할 일이라는 의견을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to express an opinion that something should be done.

phrases.example: 학교 수준을 고르게 맞추는 게 목표예요.
phrases.en: The goal is to bring the schools to an even level.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜻이 비슷하지만 더 쉬운 일상적인 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar in meaning but plainer and more everyday.

phrases.example: 모든 학교를 평준화하지 않는 나라도 있어요.
phrases.en: Some countries don't equalize all their schools.
phrases.nuance_ko: 부정형으로 다른 방식을 설명할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form is used to describe an alternative approach.

explain_en: Rather than simply 'making the same', it suggests reducing gaps in level to make things even. It is used when bringing things with gaps, such as schools, wages or service, to a similar level. The resulting state is called '평준화'.

en: to be abolished; to be repealed; to be discontinued

examples.en: That old rule is being abolished this year.
The show was cancelled because it was not popular.

examples.ko: 이 버스 노선은 다음 달에 폐지될 거예요.
examples.en: This bus route will be discontinued next month.

examples.ko: 폐지되는 제도가 많아서 안내문이 자주 나와요.
examples.en: Many systems are being abolished, so notices come out often.

examples.ko: 법이 폐지되고 나서 사람들의 생활이 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: After the law was repealed, people's lives changed.
The exam system was abolished, and the students were happy.

explain: 법, 제도, 서비스, 프로그램이 더 이상 없어질 때 써요. 가게나 회사가 문을 닫는 일은 '폐업하다', '문을 닫다'라고 해요. 사람이 없애면 '폐지하다', 없어지는 쪽이 주어면 '폐지되다'예요.

phrases.example: 이 서비스는 다음 달에 폐지될 예정이에요.
phrases.en: This service is going to be discontinued next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 없어질 계획을 알릴 때 써요. 공지문에 자주 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to announce something that will end in the future. Common in notices.

phrases.en: That system hasn't been abolished yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 아직 남아 있다는 뜻의 부정형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, meaning it still exists.

phrases.en: That old rule is gone.
phrases.nuance_ko: '폐지되다'보다 쉽고 일상적인 말이에요. 공식적인 느낌은 약해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more everyday than 'pyejidoeda', with a less formal feel.

explain_en: Passive — laws, systems, or services officially ended (규칙이 폐지되다) Used when a law, system, service or program ceases to exist. A shop or company closing is '폐업하다' or '문을 닫다' instead. The one who ends it does '폐지하다'; the thing that ends is '폐지되다'.

t90.ax: That old rule is being abolished this year.

examples.ko: 부모님이 도와주시는 걸 당연시하면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You shouldn't take it for granted that your parents help you.
People take a convenient life too much for granted.

examples.ko: 그는 남의 친절을 당연시하는 버릇이 있어요.
examples.en: He has a habit of taking other people's kindness for granted.

examples.ko: 야근을 당연시했던 분위기가 이제 바뀌고 있어요.
examples.en: The atmosphere that took overtime for granted is now changing.

examples.ko: 감사하는 마음을 잃고 모든 걸 당연시하게 됐어요.
examples.en: I lost my sense of gratitude and started taking everything for granted.

examples.ko: 여자니까 집안일을 해야 한다고 당연시하지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't assume as a given that she must do housework because she is a woman.

explain: '~을/를 당연시하다' 형태로 쓰고, 고마워해야 할 일을 그냥 당연하게 여긴다는 비판의 느낌이 자주 있어요. 일상 대화에서는 '당연하게 여기다'라고도 많이 말해요.

phrases.en: Don't take your friend's help for granted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '당연시하다' 대신 더 자주 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The more common everyday way to say 당연시하다.

phrases.en: These days working late is taken for granted.
phrases.nuance_ko: 피동형이라서 사회에서 그렇게 여겨진다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, meaning something is generally taken for granted in society.

phrases.en: A taken-for-granted attitude is not good.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에 붙여서 그런 태도나 생각을 비판할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Placed before a noun to criticize that kind of attitude.

explain_en: It is used as '~을/를 당연시하다' and often carries a hint of criticism, as in not being grateful for something. In everyday talk people also say '당연하게 여기다'.

examples.ko: 후기를 너무 맹신하면 실망할 수 있어요.
examples.en: If you trust reviews too blindly, you may be disappointed.

examples.ko: 저는 유명 블로거의 말을 맹신하지 않아요.
examples.en: I don't blindly trust what famous bloggers say.
My parents blindly believe health food ads.

examples.ko: 친구가 한 말을 그대로 맹신해서 실수했어요.
examples.en: I blindly believed what my friend said and made a mistake.
You shouldn't blindly trust an AI's answers.
It was foolish of me to trust him blindly.

explain: '~을/를 맹신하다' 형태로 쓰고, 믿으면 안 되는 것을 따져 보지 않고 믿는다는 비판의 느낌이 있어요. 부정형 '맹신하지 마세요'처럼 조언할 때도 자주 써요.

phrases.en: Don't trust online reviews too blindly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 조심하라고 조언할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to advise someone to be careful.

phrases.en: There are surprisingly many people who blindly believe in fortune-telling.
phrases.nuance_ko: '맹신하는'은 뒤에 오는 명사를 꾸며서 사람을 비판적으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: '맹신하는' describes the noun after it, criticizing the person.

phrases.en: I used to blindly believe that person's words.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과거에 따져 보지 않고 믿었다고 후회하는 느낌으로 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Said with a sense of regret about having believed without question.

explain_en: It is used as '~을/를 맹신하다' and carries a note of criticism, believing something without questioning. It is also common in advice like '맹신하지 마세요' (don't trust blindly).

en: to be denied; to be negated; to be refuted

examples.en: My opinion was completely rejected, so I was upset.
That possibility hasn't been ruled out yet.
That theory was disproved by new research.

examples.ko: 노력이 부정되는 느낌이 들 때가 있어요.
examples.en: Sometimes I feel as if my effort is being denied.
If the facts are denied, we need to investigate again.

examples.ko: 부정된 줄 알았던 소문이 다시 나왔어요.
examples.en: A rumor I thought had been denied came up again.

explain: 어떤 주장이나 가능성이 '아니다'로 받아들여질 때 써요. 사람이 말하는 '부정하다'와 짝이고, 주어가 의견이나 이론이에요. '부정'은 '아닌 것'이라는 뜻 말고 옳지 않은 일(부정행위)이라는 뜻의 같은 소리 말도 있어서 문장을 봐야 해요.

phrases.en: That possibility hasn't been ruled out yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 완전히 아니라고 하지는 못했다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means it has not been fully dismissed.

phrases.en: Let's listen again to opinions that were rejected.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 앞에서 꾸밀 때 쓰는 형태예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form used to modify a noun that follows.

phrases.en: That theory was completely disproved by an experiment.
phrases.nuance_ko: '완전히'를 붙여 전부 아니라고 받아들여졌음을 강조해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 완전히 stresses that it was rejected entirely.

explain_en: Passive: an idea or value is shown invalid or overturned. Use it when a claim or possibility ends up being treated as not true. It pairs with 부정하다, and the subject is an opinion or theory. There is also a same-sounding 부정 meaning dishonest acts (부정행위), so read the context.

gh: a claim or charge is denied or rejected

p.n: 부인되다 sounds like someone denied it, not that evidence disproved it.

t90.ax: That theory was disproved by new research.

en: to equal; to be comparable with; to rank with

examples.ko: 그 신인의 노래 실력은 프로 가수에 비견할 만해요.
examples.en: That rookie's singing is comparable to a professional singer's.
This work rivals world-famous masterpieces.

examples.ko: 그 식당의 맛은 일류 호텔에 비견해도 손색없어요.
examples.en: That restaurant's food holds up even next to a top hotel's.

examples.ko: 이 도시의 발전 속도는 어느 나라에도 비견하기 어려워요.
examples.en: This city's pace of development is hard to match with any country.
Many people compare him to Mozart.
No one can match his courage.

explain: 보통 '~에 비견하다'처럼 조사 '에'와 함께 쓰고, '비견할 만하다', '비견하기 어렵다' 꼴이 많아요. '비교하다'는 그냥 견주어 보는 것이지만, '비견하다'는 대등하게 어깨를 나란히 할 만하다는 칭찬의 느낌이에요. 말보다는 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요.

phrases.en: His skill is comparable to his senior's.
phrases.nuance_ko: 견줄 수 있을 만큼 대단하다고 칭찬할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A compliment saying something is good enough to be compared.

phrases.en: That player is compared to a legendary player.
phrases.nuance_ko: '비견하다'의 피동형으로, 어떤 사람이나 작품이 훌륭한 대상과 견주어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used when someone or something is likened to a great standard.

phrases.example: 그 경치는 어디에도 비견할 수 없어요.
phrases.en: That scenery cannot be compared to anywhere else.
phrases.nuance_ko: 견줄 것이 하나도 없다고 강하게 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A strong statement that nothing compares.

explain_en: It is usually used with the particle '에', as in '~에 비견하다', and often appears as '비견할 만하다' or '비견하기 어렵다'. While '비교하다' simply means to compare, '비견하다' praises something as being on a par with another. It is more common in writing and the news than in speech.

en: to die down; to subside; to fade away

examples.en: The flames are slowly dying down.
I'll wait a bit until my anger dies down.

examples.ko: 인기가 사그라들어서 요즘은 그 노래를 안 들어요.
examples.en: Its popularity faded, so I don't listen to that song these days.
As night came, the fever went down.
I can feel my initial passion fading.

examples.ko: 논란이 사그라들자 가게에 손님이 다시 왔어요.
examples.en: Once the controversy subsided, customers came back to the shop.

explain: 불, 열, 화, 인기처럼 센 것이 서서히 약해질 때 써요. '식다'와 비슷하지만 점점 잦아드는 느낌이 더 강해요. '사그라지다'도 같은 뜻이고, 'ㄹ'이 빠져서 '사그라드는, 사그라듭니다'가 돼요.

phrases.en: The popularity gradually died down.
phrases.nuance_ko: '사그라들다'와 같은 뜻이고 말할 때 더 자주 쓰는 편이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as '사그라들다', and a bit more common in speech.

phrases.en: After the game ended, the excitement of cheering faded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뜨겁던 분위기가 천천히 식을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a heated atmosphere slowly cools off.

phrases.en: My anger hasn't subsided yet.
phrases.nuance_ko: 감정이나 불길이 아직 약해지지 않았다고 부정으로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The negative form, saying a feeling or fire hasn't weakened yet.

explain_en: Fire or feelings gradually dying out, ending fully. It is used when something strong, such as fire, fever, anger or popularity, gradually weakens. It is similar to '식다' (to cool down) but feels more like slowly subsiding. '사그라지다' has the same meaning, and the ㄹ drops in forms like '사그라드는' and '사그라듭니다'.
